newsitem.title: USA: AOL sees probable appeal of e-mail ruling.
newsitem.headline: AOL sees probable appeal of e-mail ruling.

text.p: America Online Inc. will probably appeal a federal court order that it stop blocking promotional electronic mail from a Philadelphia firm, an attorney for the online service firm said Friday.

"I think we're probably going to appeal, and probably move to stay (the order)," America Online attorney Michael Grow said in an interview. He said no further legal actions were taken Friday, however.

U.S. District Court Judge Charles Weiner Thursday ordered America Online not to block e-mail from Cyber Promotions Inc., which sends mass electronic mailings of promotional material, pending a November trial on a lawsuit Cyber Promotions filed against America Online.
America Online, the largest U.S. online firm, told subscribers Thursday it had denied access to mailers from five Internet sites, including three associated with Cyber Promotions.
It said it was blocking only "a handful of the most abusive junk mailers who have generated numerous member complaints."
Cyber Promotions attorney Paul Kochanski said the judge's ruling Thursday merely aimed to preserve the status quo and had no bearing on the issues to be decided in the case.

The temporary restraining order tells America Online not to block Cyber Promotions mailings to "recipients who wish to receive the mail," and not to interefere with Cyber Promotions's business relationships with Internet service providers.
Mailings from Cyber Promotions contain provisions describing how recipients can remove themselves from the company's mailing list, Kochanski said.
Separately, America Online said it planned to list its common stock on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol "AOL," beginning Monday, Sept. 16.
The stock currently trades on the Nasdaq, where it edged down 18.75 cents to $28.3125.
